title: Payer Filing and Appeal Limits for Wound Care Dressings
content:
# Payer filing and appeal limits — Wound Care Supply Program

The limits below govern claims and appeals for every tier of the Wound Care Supply Program. All limits are in calendar days.

| Tier | Timely filing of an original claim | Corrected claim after a CO-16 denial | First-level appeal | Second-level appeal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wound Care Self-Pay Program | 0 (no payer claim is filed) | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (no payer appeal exists) | 0 (none) |
| Wound Care Commercial HMO Program | 90 | 90 | 180 | 120 |
| Wound Care Commercial PPO Program | 180 | 180 | 180 | 120 |
| Wound Care Medicare Advantage Program | 180 | 180 | 65 | 0 (the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity automatically) |
| Wound Care Original Medicare Program | 365 | 365 | 120 | 180 |
| Wound Care Medicaid Program | 365 | 365 | 60 | 120 |

## What each column counts from

- **Timely filing**: the payer limit for an original claim, counted from the date of service, which is the ship date. A figure of 0 means no payer claim is filed on the tier.
- **Corrected claim**: the window for submitting a corrected claim after an unprocessable (CO-16) denial, counted from the posting date of that denial. A figure of 0 means not applicable.
- **First-level appeal**: the window for filing the first-level appeal, counted from the posting date of the denial. The first level is the commercial internal appeal, the Medicare Advantage reconsideration, the Medicare redetermination or the Medicaid plan appeal. A figure of 0 means no payer appeal exists.
- **Second-level appeal**: the window for filing the second-level appeal, counted from the posting date of the first-level appeal decision. The second level is the commercial external review, the Medicare QIC reconsideration or the Medicaid state fair hearing. A figure of 0 means there is no customer-filed second level: on the self-pay tier there is none, and on the Medicare Advantage tier the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity automatically.

## Comparing the tiers

- The two commercial tiers share the same appeal windows (180 days at the first level, 120 at the second) but differ in filing: 90 days on the commercial HMO tier against 180 on the commercial PPO tier.
- The shortest first-level appeal window is the 60 days of the Wound Care Medicaid Program; the Medicare Advantage tier allows 65.
- On every insured tier the corrected-claim window equals the timely-filing figure of the same tier.
